transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-10
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (VectraHead Platform), Liam O'Connor (SRE), Marta Ruiz (Product), Jon (Dev)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Agree to 5% canary, telemetry thresholds, runbook delivery.

00:00 Sofia: okay, welcome everyone, thanks for carving out the time this afternoon. agenda is short — finalize the traffic orchestration, canary thresholds, and ops handoff details. any additions?
00:14 Priya: sounds good. wanted to make sure we cover the A/B metrics, like quality delta vs cost — those are key to product's go decision.
00:25 Ethan: we'll show the proposed ramp and the telemetry we'll collect. also quick note — we ran a baseline yesterday with quantized variant, results were consistent but slightly higher latency (uhm) by about 8ms on p99.
00:40 Liam: can we dig into p99 and error budget? our SLO is 200ms p95 for user-facing endpoints, but p99 is a secondary guardrail.
00:52 Sofia: yes, so proposal: 5% rolling canary, hold 48 hours, monitor three buckets: latency, error-rate, and semantic-regression (quality). immediate rollback if latency p95 > 250ms for >5 minutes or semantic-regression alert triggers.
01:12 Marta: what do you mean by semantic-regression alert? how automated is that?
01:20 Ethan: good q. we have automated eval hooks: a prompt-set of 120 golden prompts. we measure rouge/f1-style scores and a heuristics-based hallucination classifier. threshold set at a 3% drop relative to baseline triggers an alert. human-in-loop validation within 30 minutes recommended before final rollback unless it's egregious.
01:46 Priya: I want clarity — we don't want constant false positives. can we have a severity bucket? like P0 immediate rollback, P1 page on-call and hold, P2 ticket and monitor.
01:58 Sofia: absolutely. propose mapping: P0 = hallucination rate > 1% absolute on critical prompts or production-safety trigger, auto-failover; P1 = quality drop 3-6% — page SE and stand by; P2 = <3% — create ticket and watch.
02:18 Jon (Dev): small interjection, for A/B where do we log which user saw which variant? need traceability for debugging.
02:27 Ethan: good point — we annotate responses with opaque route_id and model_variant metadata, all stored in our request logs that Vectra can ingest via S3/CloudWatch. we'll avoid PII.
02:40 Liam: about data retention — legal asked for 90 day retention on logs for the pilot. is that default?
02:48 Sofia: by default hosted keeps 30 days for logs; for the pilot we can extend to 90 days with redwood retention add-on, it's in the contract. redwood private customers can set within VPC.
03:05 Marta: security checklist — what's left? SSO? KMS? SOC2?
03:12 Sofia: we provided the security pack last week: SOC2 attestation, SAML SSO integration pattern, KMS for model keys is supported. outstanding: you asked for HSM/KMS integration proof-of-concept, E2E audit log sample — Ethan has a sample audit payload.
03:30 Ethan: i'll send the HSM integration notes and a sample audit-event in the slack thread after the call.
03:36 Priya: perfect. back to canary — are we doing a pure canary or A/B test with 50/50 for quality comparison?
03:45 Sofia: primary cut is a canary ramp — 5% -> 20% -> 50% over two days if all metrics pass. we'll run a parallel A/B for a 10% slice to measure per-session quality vs current baseline for a week in the beta lane if you want deeper comparisons.
04:05 Priya: okay that works. can we define exact ramp durations?
04:10 Ethan: propose: initial 5% for 6 hours, if no P0/P1 then 20% over next 6 hours, then 50% for 36 hours. total watch 48 hours at meaningful traffic. the A/B 10% extra runs concurrently but only samples requests for the eval set.
04:34 Liam: what about KV cache / prefix caching? we saw cache-hit variance during tests.
04:40 Ethan: during the baseline we disabled prefix cache to measure cold starts, for production we'll enable prefix/KV caching. for the canary we'll mirror production caching behavior except for one test run with cache disabled to detect regressions.
04:58 Jon: does the routing support gradual KV warmup? we want not to spike backend.
05:05 Ethan: yes, the runtime handles warmed caches and the gateway will throttle bursts. we'll include a burst-policy to cap initial RPS increase to 10% per minute.
05:20 Marta: monitoring — dashboard links? we tried to open the Grafana link but it timed out last night.
05:28 Sofia: Ethan pushed a read-only dashboard. i'll re-share the links right after this call. expect: latency panels (p50/p95/p99), model tokens-per-request, hallucination rate, top 20 prompts failing QA, cost per 1k tokens.
05:45 Ethan: also added a synthetic traffic synthetic that hits the golden prompt set every 5m.
05:52 Priya: alerts — what severity maps to page?
05:57 Liam: we want pages for P0 and P1; P2 should create ticket only. Page rotation: primary SRE (Liam) then Redwood SE.
06:07 Sofia: noted. we'll provide an Alertmanager rule set as a starting point.
06:12 Marta: rollbacks — fully automated rollback? manual?
06:17 Ethan: plan is semi-automated: P0 auto-rollback will flip traffic to previous model variant and page on-call. P1 will pause ramp and require a manual approval to proceed or rollback. P2 is observation.
06:32 Priya: legal wants a freeze window during full cutover — minimum 2-hour quiet window at midnight PT. can we do that?
06:41 Sofia: yes, we can schedule a quiet window. who will coordinate?
06:45 Priya: i'll coordinate internally. target cutover date tentatively 2027-02-20, quiet window 02:00-04:00 PT TBD.
06:55 Liam: oh, one more — what about cost alerting? if cost / 1k tokens spikes 30% we'll want to be notified.
07:03 Ethan: added cost per 1k tokens panel and a composite alert rule. we can send cost alerts to Slack only, not page.
07:10 Marta: DRY RUN — how do we simulate failover?
07:15 Ethan: we have a dry-run script that will run synthetic load and then inject a latency bump on worker nodes to simulate degradation, observing the circuit breaker. Redwood to run the first dry run in staging with you on 2027-02-18.
07:31 Sofia: ok, so next steps are clear — dry run, run load test, finalize runbook. any other blockers?
07:38 Priya: audit log format needs to show request_id, route_id, model_variant, timestamp, and response hash. ensure no PII.
07:49 Ethan: sample will include all except response payload. we'll send the sample.
07:56 Jon: small nit, for A/B experiment labeling, we'll need consistent cookies or header annotation to avoid skew.
08:03 Ethan: we'll use a sticky header for experiment routing to keep user sessions consistent across ramp.
08:10 Marta: ok if we do 5% canary, what's the expected impact on latency for end-users?
08:17 Ethan: based on baseline, expected p95 change is <10ms. p99 could vary more during cache warm-up but with prefix caching it'll stabilize.
08:27 Liam: our SRE wants to know how to escalate post-cutover if we see an unexplained increase in hallucinations.
08:34 Sofia: escalation path: page on-call SRE (Liam), Redwood SE (Ethan), then Redwood infra on-call. Runbook includes sample play-by-play.
08:43 Priya: let's call out stakeholders — Product owns quality decisions, Platform owns rollout timing, Redwood owns the runtime and rollback automation.
08:53 Sofia: perfect. any outstanding integrations or compliance items?
08:58 Priya: HSM proof-of-concept — legal will need evidence.
09:02 Ethan: will share HSM notes and a small test harness.
09:08 Sofia: okay final check — do we have consensus on thresholds? restating: auto-roll on P0 (hallucinations >1% or safety hit), auto-fail if p95 > 250ms for more than 5 minutes, pause on P1 (3-6% quality drop), P2 monitor. A/B to run 10% sample for one week after initial canary to measure cost/quality delta. agreed?
09:30 Priya: agreed.
09:33 Liam: agreed.
09:35 Marta: agreed.
09:36 Sofia: great. i'll follow up with runbook and one-page rollback. Ethan will run burst load and share dashboards. Priya will confirm quiet window.
09:45 Sofia: any final questions?
09:48 Jon: none from dev.
09:50 Sofia: thanks everyone. we'll meet after dry run for a short retrospective.
09:55 Meeting end.

Notes: transcript contains occasional ASR errors; speaker 'Jon' labelled informally in recording. Links referenced: (1) Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.example/vectra-readonly (redacted) (2) Cutover runbook draft: /shared/drive/vectra/cutover-runbook-draft.pdf (to be published).
